findings.title: Refund endpoint lacks requireAdmin; any logged-in user can refund any order
findings.explanation: The PR says the new POST /orders/:id/refund is for admins, but line 31 registers it with only `requireUser`. The sibling admin action on line 30 (`cancel`) also uses `requireAdmin`. `refundOrder` (lines 18-26) never checks role or ownership: it loads any order by id and calls `queueRefund` for the remaining amount. So any authenticated user can trigger full refunds on paid orders, including orders that belong to other users. That causes direct financial loss.
findings.reasoningSummary: Route registration omits the requireAdmin middleware used by the other admin route, and the handler has no authorization check of its own.
findings.suggestedFix: Register as router.post("/orders/:id/refund", requireUser, requireAdmin, refundOrder).

findings.title: Refund endpoint lacks requireAdmin; any authenticated user can refund any paid order

The sibling admin action `/orders/:id/cancel` does include it. `refundOrder` itself never checks `req.user.isAdmin` and never checks that the order belongs to the caller. findings.suggestedFix: Register the route as `router.post("/orders/:id/refund", requireUser, requireAdmin, refundOrder);`.

findings.title: Reopen can turn a refunded order back into "paid" while it stays fully refunded
findings.explanation: cancelOrder sets status to "cancelled" no matter what the current status is, so a refunded order can be cancelled. reopenOrder then sets any cancelled order to "paid" without checking refundedCents. The result is an order with status "paid" and refundedCents == totalCents. Per the reopen comment, that order can now ship again even though the customer was refunded in full. The order history is also lost.
findings.reasoningSummary: refunded -> cancelled (via cancel) -> paid (via reopen) leaves a paid order with full refund recorded.
findings.suggestedFix: In reopenOrder, refuse when order.refundedCents > 0. Also track the pre-cancel status, or have cancel reject refunded orders.
